summary: Raised from MPI-631. Two asymmetries found while fixing the gallery's VRAM retention. (1) Images got thumbnails and videos never did: MPI-319 gave images a 512px WebP because decoding full-res PNGs in cards was ~179x heavier, but a video card's 256px poster is THROWN AWAY on promotion and replaced with the full-res master - so a 3000x1280 clip in a ~300px card decodes ~100x the pixels the card shows. (2) One thumb size serves every card size: at slider level 4 the grid targets 2 cards per row, so on a wide window a card is ~950-1250px painted from a 512px source, and ffmpegThumb.js:9 still claims that size is 'sharp enough at the biggest gallery card' - true for whatever window it was measured in, false on Fabio's. Fabio proposed capping the max card size instead; rejected in the brief because the screen's pixel count is fixed (2 big cards or 6 small ones fill the same monitor), so size-matched renditions keep memory roughly flat AND fix quality, whereas a cap removes a feature to work around a fixable derivative and, by his own observation, forces MORE cards resident. MPI-631's trigger C is what makes a larger tier affordable at all: only the visible band is resident now.

ID CORRECTION: this card was written up as MPI-632 in the MPI-631 close-out event before it was allocated, and it is MPI-633. Self-inflicted and harmless: the brief was written with the Write tool to tasks/MPI-632/brief.md BEFORE createTask ran, and that write created the directory - which is exactly what the mkdir lock in the createTask recipe is for, so os.mkdir on 632 raised FileExistsError and the loop moved to 633. Nobody else's card was touched (tasks/MPI-632 was untracked and held only that one file), the stray directory is removed and the brief now sits in tasks/MPI-633/. The lesson for the next agent: allocate the id FIRST, then write the card's files - a Write to tasks/<id>/ is enough to consume the id you were about to claim. The MPI-631 task.moved event above still says 'Follow-up raised as MPI-632'; event logs are append-only, so it is corrected here rather than rewritten.

todo -> doing. Picked up from handoff 95bd9759 (MPI-631 closed and measured). checklist.md and files.json written; the card claims services/ffmpegThumb.js, routes/projects.js, js/services/projectService.js, MpiGalleryGrid.js, the two rendition tests, docs/gallery.md and docs/releases/UNRELEASED.md. Work starts at Phase 0, NOT at code: the brief's decode-cost claim (a 3000x1280 clip in a ~300px card decodes ~100x the pixels it shows) is reasoned from how browsers decode video and has never been sampled, so M1 (per-video VRAM against resolution) picks the proxy size and M2 (gallery VRAM at slider level 1 vs level 4 on TODAY's build) establishes the flatness the brief's table asserts as arithmetic. Both are acceptance criteria. Noted while claiming: the file-claim record ab0f51bf-095f-4c37-9c54-90f90844b263 still holds MpiGalleryGrid.js for MPI-573, which is in done, with a heartbeat of 2026-08-22 - a stale claim, not a live peer.

Phase 0 measured, before any rendition code, and it changed the design. M1 (per-video VRAM against native resolution, one app launch per config, engine off): cost tracks native pixels at roughly 20 MB per megapixel per promoted video - 3000x1280 costs 65-81 MB per card, 1280x800 costs 8-24, 1152x720 costs 11-21, so a 720p proxy is a 6x cut, not the 100x the brief reasoned from pixel counts. M1b: the same clip in a 64x80 box and a 134x167 box costs the same within noise across 4.4x the painted area, so decode cost really is native-resolution-driven and display size does not enter it - the mechanism the card rests on is confirmed. M2 (120 image cards, MPI-631 tour): the brief's flatness table is wrong by an order of magnitude and today's build is flat the OTHER way - largest card size costs 12 MB against 34-42 MB at the smallest, because it holds fewer cards at the same 512px source. Serving a 1280px rendition at the largest size costs 238 MB. The control that matters: the SAME config without scrolling costs 23.7 MB, so 214 of those MB are Chromium's GPU image cache retaining every card the scroll passed, not the working set. That is the same class of problem MPI-631 fixed for video, so the ladder needs an image-side demote on the existing DEMOTE_MARGIN_PX observer; added to the checklist as Phase 1b. Two measurement traps recorded in validation.md, each of which produced a confident wrong number first: the standard desktop harness sets CUBRIC_E2E, which main.js turns into disable-gpu, so every VRAM sample reads 0.0 MB on a healthy app; and Win32_Process reports NO children for the Electron main pid, so a process-tree sampler also reads 0.0 - the pid list has to come from app.getAppMetrics().

doing -> done. Shipped in 6eff5708 + bb46386e, confirmed live by Fabio ("VRAM is stable, images look good, videos are good"). What shipped: a two-tier image rendition ladder (512 + 1280) picked by the card's RENDERED BOX in device pixels and clamped to the source, so a 1280x800 asset gets no derivative and a big card mounts filePath; and a 720p video hover proxy with audio, wired through one helper that all five video routes call. Backfill widened and renamed to /backfill-media-derivatives; GC and delete now match <id>.thumb.* / <id>.proxy.* by prefix. The design reversal, which is the part worth carrying forward: Phase 1b was built on the inference that the 214 MB gap between a scrolled and an unscrolled run was retention a scroll-out demote would return. It is not. Measured in one run: 236.5 MB with the demote firing against 234.5 without it, while every off-screen card had genuinely swapped back to its 512 thumb. Chromium keys a decoded image by URL and holds it with no live reference, and no page API evicts it. The lever is how many distinct large renditions are ever PAINTED, so promoteImage now refuses while _isScrolling and the existing 150 ms scroll-idle timer sweeps the resting band. A fling past 120 cards paints 6 instead of 120: 73.8 MB against 241.5, where the no-scroll floor is 72.9. L1 fell to 14.3 from today's 34-42. The demote is kept for the working set, with a comment stating exactly what it does and does not buy. Verified: npm test 759/759, desktop 37/37 (both re-run at close-out, after Phase 2), eslint clean, release:check passed, 10 mutations all RED. Raw rig output is INLINED in validation.md because the rigs and their scratchpad logs were deleted with the card. Left open deliberately: no rig run over a gallery of PROXIED clips. M1 measured the resolution curve directly so the per-card saving is known (~6x); the whole-gallery number is not sampled. Not carded - raise one if it matters.
